headline: Korea-Japan Currency Swap Extended 3 Years, $10 Billion
summary: South Korea and Japan agreed to extend their $10 billion currency swap agreement by three years. The decision was reached by finance officials at the G20 and IMF annual meetings, stressing foreign exchange liquidity.
why: Currency swap lines let central banks or governments exchange currencies in a crisis, providing dollar and yen liquidity. They are a key backstop for foreign exchange stability in Asia.
